top_choice_rationale: Palladium-catalyzed C-N coupling to Buchwald and Hartwig has a clear mechanistic principle (ligand control of amido-palladium reductive elimination), about three decades of independent confirmation and routine process-scale use, and a clean two-name allocation. The word 'general' in the citation separates it from the narrow 1983 Migita/Kosugi tin-amide reaction, and the C-N bottleneck differs from the C-C couplings honored in 2010. Targeted protein degradation is the more novel capability but has no approved drug and a credit boundary (glue versus PROTAC strands) that three names cannot cover, so it ranks second; no award ranks last because a mature, well-attributed achievement exists.
